title: Announcement Orchestra: Runbook for Sequenced Channels, Content Handoffs, and Post-Launch Signals
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a deterministic, low-friction runbook to coordinate a sequenced public announcement across blog, product email, social, and webinar. The runbook must define ownership for each asset, timing windows (embargo/internal-live/public), automated checklist gates, and post-launch signal collection for early rollback/patch decisions.
objective: Reduce missed handoffs and last-minute blockers by providing a single source-of-truth schedule and handoff checklist for all announcement channels; enable rapid post-launch monitoring and decisioning across PM/Comms/Design/Eng.
scope: Includes schedule templates, channel-specific asset checklists (blog, email, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, webinar deck + registration flow), required approvals, and a lightweight post-launch signal dashboard spec. Will include example timelines for staged rollouts (region-first, canary customers, GA).
out_of_scope: Paid ad creative, partner co-marketing contracts, long-form sell sheets for sales enablement (these will be referenced but owned by Growth/Sales).
deliverables: Automated pre-launch checklist (Notion template + Slack notif)
Post-launch signals spec and dashboard mock (Looker/Console)

notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: We recommend a 2-phase public announcement (canary customers then GA) to protect customer experience; this delays full GA by 48-72 hours but reduces blast risk.
Decision: Use existing release-notes canonical markdown in repo rather than a bespoke CMS; reduces integration work but will require an explicit mapping step for Console release notes widget.

Open risk: If model quantization recommendations change after blog is drafted, we'll need a short Triage note and a blog addendum. Plan to reserve a 'technical appendix' area in the blog for last-minute benchmark swaps.

Day 0: T+0-6h monitor alerts and high-priority support queue for critical regressions

Day 3: Post-launch debrief (all stakeholders) and decide on follow-up comms or rollbacks
Day 7: Publish lessons learned and update runbook based on what failed/passed
